backlink_pages.title: Runbook — Webhook DLQ Replay
backlink_pages.author: Sam Ortiz
backlink_pages.excerpt: When to use Webhook delivery retries exhaust the DLQ without surfacing a final failure event—that symptom is NMA-105. The longer-term runbook and tooling work is tracked as NMA-162. Steps Confirm

backlink_pages.title: Observability Standards
backlink_pages.author: Jordan Lee
backlink_pages.excerpt: Tracing Webhook fan-out traces under NMA-170 use the shared trace context. Worker crashes when payloads contain nested null optional fields—see NMA-108—must include job type attributes on the span.

backlink_pages.title: Component Map — Platform API
backlink_pages.author: Jordan Lee
backlink_pages.excerpt: Platform surface REST API, Webhooks, Workers, SDK, and Rate Limiting share auth middleware and request IDs. Failures often span two components—treat the map as a dependency graph, not a folder list.

content.text: Production rollout complete; runbook updated with example trace queries.
Webhook fan-out and fan-in paths lack distributed traces, so multi-hop delivery delays are hard to attribute.
Add OpenTelemetry traces around fan-out dispatch and fan-in aggregation, including delivery id and destination host attributes.
Sample aggressively in staging and at the standard production rate so dashboards remain affordable.
